summary: Laos admits fellow ASEAN nationals visa-free for up to 30 days (14 for Myanmar), plus Japan, South Korea, Russia, Switzerland and others on bilateral or unilateral waivers. Nearly everyone else gets a 30-day tourist visa easily — online through the official Lao eVisa or on arrival at major airports and border crossings. About 35 nationalities that are not on the eVisa list, mostly in Africa and the Middle East plus Pakistan, Bangladesh and Iran, should apply at a Lao embassy.

travelInsurance.text: No official source makes insurance a condition of entry. The UK government advises adequate travel health insurance: medical care is basic, there are no reliable facilities for emergencies outside Vientiane, and medical evacuation is difficult to organise and very expensive.

declarations.name: Lao Digital Immigration Form (LDIF)
declarations.submitWindow: Within 3 days before arrival, and again within 3 days before departure
declarations.text: Since 1 September 2025, every foreign national entering or leaving through Wattay International Airport (Vientiane), Luang Prabang International Airport, Pakse International Airport or the first Lao-Thai Friendship Bridge must register on the Lao Digital Immigration Form at immigration.gov.la within 3 days before arrival and again before departure. At those four checkpoints it replaces the paper arrival and departure cards; at other crossings, fill in the paper card.

source.name: Department of Immigration of the Lao PDR — News: Lao Digital Immigration Form (LDIF)

currencyLimits.text: No official Lao source we could read publishes a cash-declaration threshold or the rules on taking kip out of the country. Declare large sums on arrival and ask Lao Customs before carrying them.

notes: Drug offenses carry severe penalties in Laos, including the death penalty for trafficking.
Antiques and Buddha images require an export permit. Buy religious artefacts only from licensed dealers.

payments.text: Cash is essential. Cards work in upmarket hotels and some city restaurants, and ATMs in towns charge fees with low withdrawal caps. Thai baht and US dollars are widely accepted for larger purchases.

safety.text: Most visits are trouble-free; petty theft, bag-snatching by people on motorbikes and road accidents are the main risks. The UK Foreign Office advises against all but essential travel to Xaisomboun Province, where there have been attacks on infrastructure and armed clashes with anti-government groups, and urges extreme caution in Bokeo Province near the Golden Triangle. Landmines and unexploded weapons are a hazard throughout Laos, so keep to main routes in rural areas.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Laos travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: November to February is the cool, dry season — ideal for Luang Prabang, Vientiane and the south. March to May is very hot and hazy from field burning, and June to October brings monsoon rain.

idp.text: Laos is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

source.name: UN Treaty Collection — Convention on Road Traffic (Geneva, 1949), status of parties
source.instrument: Convention on Road Traffic, Geneva, 19 September 1949 (UNTS vol. 125, p. 3)

driving.text: Laos is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Laos yet.

source.name: UN Treaty Collection — Convention on Road Traffic (Geneva, 1949), status of parties
source.instrument: Convention on Road Traffic, Geneva, 19 September 1949 (UNTS vol. 125, p. 3)

tips.text: Bring crisp US dollar notes. They pay for the visa on arrival, are accepted for many tourist services, and are a useful backup where ATMs are unreliable.

The Lao eVisa is accepted only at designated entry points — Vientiane and Luang Prabang airports and a handful of land crossings such as the first Friendship Bridge. Check the official list before planning an overland entry.
Unexploded ordnance from the 1960s-70s still contaminates parts of eastern and southern Laos. Stay on marked paths and roads in rural areas and never touch metal objects found on the ground.
The kip has depreciated sharply in recent years, so prices for tours and hotels are often quoted in US dollars or Thai baht. Carry a mix and check which currency a quote is in.
Cover shoulders and knees at temples, remove shoes before entering, and be discreet during the dawn alms round in Luang Prabang. Keep your distance and never disrupt the monks.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Laos?
faq.answer: ASEAN nationals enter visa-free (30 days for most members, 14 for Myanmar), and Japan, South Korea, Switzerland, Luxembourg, Russia and Mongolia have bilateral or unilateral waivers. Almost everyone else — including US, UK, EU, Canadian and Australian passport holders — gets a 30-day tourist visa either online via laoevisa.gov.la or on arrival at major entry points. Nationalities missing from the eVisa list should apply at a Lao embassy.

faq.question: Should I get the Lao eVisa or a visa on arrival?
faq.answer: Both give a 30-day single-entry tourist stay. The eVisa (USD 50, about three business days online) skips the arrival line but is accepted only at designated checkpoints; the visa on arrival is paid in cash at the border, with a passport photo, and is available at all major airports and border crossings. No official page publishes its fee.

faq.question: Can I use the Lao eVisa at any border crossing?
faq.answer: No. It is honored only at designated entry points, including Vientiane's Wattay and Luang Prabang international airports and the first Lao-Thai Friendship Bridge. Arriving anywhere else, get a visa on arrival or an embassy visa instead; check the current list on laoevisa.gov.la.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Laos?
faq.answer: Yes. Tourist visas can be extended at most twice per arrival, for a total of up to 60 additional days, at the Department of Immigration in Vientiane or a provincial immigration office. Apply at least 3 days before your stay expires; the fee is 20,000 kip per day plus 40,000 kip per application, and it takes 1-2 business days. Visa-exempt stays cannot normally be extended. Overstays are fined per day on departure.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Laos?
faq.answer: Yes. US passport holders are not visa-exempt. Apply online for the Lao eVisa (USD 50) before travel or obtain a 30-day tourist visa on arrival for a cash fee at major airports and border crossings.
